note: Parodies of the rest of the real UFC rankings (generated from tools/roster_full_src.py). Sporting jokes only.

fighters.bio: Six foot seven of patient kickboxing. Has been the next big thing for so long he's now the current big thing.
Ends fights so fast the broadcast has to replay the walkout to fill time.
Former college footballer who tackles people for a living now and gets paid more for it.
Used to drive a school bus. Now drives heavyweights into the canvas, with the same calm.
A heavyweight who wrestles like a lightweight and eats like three.
Throws every punch like he's mad at it personally.
Big, patient and slightly shy, until he's on top of you. Then very loud.
Croatian heavyweight with a chin made of the Adriatic coastline.
Former model who decided faces were for punching. Including, mostly, other people's.
Trained in Thailand and came back kicking legs like they owed him money.
City Kickboxing product with a jab that arrives before the bell does.
Built like a statue, talks like a stand-up comedian, fights like a car crash.
Southpaw who puts people to sleep and then tells them about it on his podcast.
Undefeated, unbothered and allergic to wasting a single strike.
Ex-champion with legendary 'Polish Power' and an even more legendary love of cake.
Southpaw striker who once nearly took the throne from the GOAT and has been chasing that night since.
Long, patient and precise. Picks people apart like he's paid by the inch.
Chokes people out with the calm of a man doing his taxes.
Undefeated in the big show for so long they ran out of ways to say 'still undefeated'.
Philly power puncher who calls himself Bodybagz and works very hard to keep the name accurate.
Jiu-jitsu black belt who mostly uses it as a reason not to worry about getting taken down.
Pressure, cardio and a nickname that lies to his opponents.
Long English kickboxer with a spinning back fist he throws mostly to see if it works.
Calls himself The Future and has a future-sized Instagram to prove it.
Muay Thai assassin who knocks men out and then poses like it's a fashion shoot.
Ecuador's undefeated hope. Hits hard, stays calm, eats rice.
Little hammer, big guillotine. Comes from a family that collects black belts.
Wrestles you into the fence and then into a choke and then into next week.
Famous for a spinning back kick so good the replay has its own fan club.
Former French special forces. Treats every round like a tactical operation with snacks.
Young Aussie who finishes fights before the commentators finish his name.
Throws spinning wheel kicks in fights like other people throw jabs.
Two-belt champ from across the water who came over to prove it wasn't a fluke. It wasn't.
Wrestles at a pace that makes opponents check if the round is over. It isn't.
Undefeated, unspectacular, unbeatable. Wins rounds the way gravity wins.
Throws everything, submits from anywhere, and smiles the entire time.
Manchester counter-puncher who makes you miss, then makes you pay, then makes you watch the replay.
Fighting Nerds disciple who fights like the nerds were wrong about him.
Kicks from angles that don't exist. Mexico's most acrobatic export.
Quiet Englishman who out-points loud men for a living.
Came back from a pink slip to beat ranked men. Very good at not giving up.
Young Argentine who throws in volume and talks about Messi between rounds.
Late bloomer who started finishing everybody in his thirties and never stopped.
Kung fu kid grown into a power puncher. Always in fights of the night.
Wins streaks so long they forget to rank him and then rank him.
Another cousin from the most dangerous family tree in sport. Striking included this time.
Throws flying knees, spinning wheel kicks and the occasional perfectly normal jab.
Patient Canadian counter-striker. Speaks softly, jabs often.
Mexico's latest striker. 1ton is already calling him the greatest of all time.
Former champion with fists like coconuts and a moustache from another century.
Starts slow, ends fast. Famous for a front kick that redecorated a face.
Youngest champion in years, throws punches like he has somewhere else to be.
Talks like a headliner, fights like one, and would like you to know both.
Chaos merchant. Will try a flying knee, a guillotine and a backflip in one round.
Okinawan grappler who chains submissions like he's practising origami.
Karate-stance legend back for one more run. Still faster than everybody.
Liverpool's undefeated flyweight with hands like a kickboxer's caffeine habit.
Kazakh wrestler who is always, somehow, on your back.
Smooth grappler with hands that surprise people who expected only grappling.
Pressure puncher with knockouts in the bag and more in the post.
Panamanian striker with long arms and a longer list of upset wins.
Veteran who wins by being in the right place 400 times a fight.
Young Brazilian with dreadlocks and a takedown that arrives without notice.
Argentine wrestler who celebrates like a footballer and wrestles like a python.
Steady striker who has fought half the division and remembers all of it.
Portuguese-based Brazilian who has never met a pressure fight she didn't enjoy.
Big, strong and polite about it.
Canadian with a wild streak and a sensible gameplan, in that order.
Volume striker who throws more than the scorers can count.
Karate-based champion with kicks you only see on the replay.
French karate star who plans fights like chess and finishes them like a hammer.
Mexico's former queen. 1ton has her poster. Several posters.
Grappling prodigy who takes backs the way other people take selfies.
Chinese striker with heavy hands and a very unlucky nickname for her opponents.
Canadian grinder who outworks everyone and then thanks them.
Has been called The Future since she was a teenager. The future is now, apparently.
Phoenix wrestler who wins rounds by being impossible to get away from.
World-class jiu-jitsu, striking that varies by the day, and armbars that do not.
Veteran grappler who submits people in ways the commentators have to look up.
Olympic-level wrestler who puts you down and keeps you there.
Holds records for submission wins and for being underestimated.
Former title challenger with a jab like a woodpecker on a deadline.
Undefeated pressure fighter who doesn't believe in slow starts.
Venezuelan grinder who turns every fight into a wrestling seminar.
Young Brazilian who swings first and takes questions later.
Japanese veteran who goes by one name and one plan: get the back.
Submission specialist with a perfect record and an imperfect nickname.
